15.0.1.s: The function swaps D[s1] and D[s2], then recurses inward on (s1+1, s2−1) until the indices meet. That **reverses** D[s1..s2]. **Option C**.

15.0.2.s:
S[i] is the length of the non-decreasing run ending at i:

| i | X[i] | compared with X[i−1] | S[i] |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6 | — | 1 |
| 2 | 3 | 6 > 3 | 1 |
| 3 | 5 | 3 ≤ 5 | 2 |
| 4 | 4 | 5 > 4 | 1 |
| 5 | 10 | 4 ≤ 10 | 2 |

The result is **[1, 1, 2, 1, 2]**. **Option C**.

15.0.3.s:
`count` returns the number of nodes in the subtree:

- nodes 3–8 are leaves: 1 each
- `count(1)` = 1 + 3 = 4
- `count(2)` = 1 + 3 = 4
- `count(0)` = 1 + 4 + 4 = **9**

**Option D**.

15.1.1.s: `A.extend(B)` appends each element of B, giving [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]. (`append` would add the whole list as one element: [1, 2, 3, [4, 5, 6]].) **Option A**.

15.2.2.s:
f(a, b) computes $a\times b$ using doubling:

| call | result |
|---|---|
| f(15, 10) | 2·f(7, 10) |
| f(7, 10) | 2·f(3, 10) |
| f(3, 10) | 2·f(1, 10) |
| f(1, 10) | 2·f(0, 10) = 2·10 = 20 |

Working back up: f(3) = 40, f(7) = 80, f(15) = **160**.

(It isn't 15 × 10, because an odd a returns 2·f((a−1)/2), dropping the extra b.)
